sara_support: FYI customer (acme-inc) opened a ticket — 403 on embeddings endpoint after key rotation. They pasted a curl that returns 403 with body {"error":"forbidden","reason":"signature_mismatch"} and header x-request-id: req_20270308_9f7c2a
customer_acme: yeah we rotated our service key yesterday. Some calls work, embedding requests fail consistently with 403. We can repro from our side, attaching curl and response.
customer_acme: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer svc_key_ABC..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
customer_acme: response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\n{"error":"forbidden","reason":"signature_mismatch"}\nx-request-id: req_20270308_9f7c2a
raj_oncall: thanks — can you paste the raw response headers and the exact Authorization header (you can redact the token body but keep prefix)? also confirm which org/project you're targeting (org id and project id shown in dashboard)
customer_acme: Org: org-acme-9, Project: proj-website-2. We used the service key created under org-acme-9 -> project default. Not sure how project mapping works.
sara_support: internal note: suspect scope mismatch across org/project or signature canonicalization differences after rotation. Need reproducible curl + server logs (x-request-id). Ask them to run curl with -v and --trace-ascii, and also to include the X-Redwood-Org and X-Redwood-Project headers in the test.
customer_acme: ok running now, output attached. includes request-id and verbose TLS handshake. They included trace but it's long.
dev_kate: quick check: if the service key was created scoped to a specific project (proj-website-2) but the request omits X-Redwood-Project or uses a different project header, server treats as cross-project and returns 403 with signature_mismatch if key scope doesn't cover target. Also some SDKs normalize base64 for signatures differently — we saw urlsafe_b64 vs standard b64 causing mismatch when clients implement signing manually.
dev_kate: repro steps I used locally: 1) create a service key scoped to proj-A 2) call embeddings endpoint but set header X-Redwood-Project: proj-B 3) send signed Authorization header created with standard base64 signing -> server logs 403 reason=scope_mismatch and server log shows signature computed vs signature provided mismatch
dev_kate: example curl used to repro locally:
```
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer svc_key_PROJ_A..." \
  -H "X-Redwood-Org: org-acme-9" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Project: proj-website-2" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```
dev_kate: when I accidentally used a mismatched project header I got:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"forbidden","reason":"scope_mismatch","hint":"service key not valid for target project"}
x-request-id: req_local_20270308_ab12
```
sara_support: OK. Action items for customer: 1) run this command (adds verbose trace and dumps headers) and paste the full output including x-request-id 2) confirm exact service key creation page (is key scoped to a project?) 3) run a repro where you explicitly set X-Redwood-Project to the project that owns the key
sara_support: curl we want them to run (copy/paste):
```
curl -v --trace-ascii debug.txt \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Org: org-acme-9" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Project: proj-website-2" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
# attach debug.txt and the raw response body (debug.txt includes headers and TLS info)
```
customer_acme: ran it, attaching debug.txt. Response included x-request-id req_20270308_9f7c2a again. Also included a snippet in the trace where Authorization header sent was Bearer svc_key_ABC... (I redacted middle). We also tried explicitly setting X-Redwood-Project and still got 403.
ops_bot: deploy-bot: noticed a small key-rotation roll forward in prod at 2027-03-08T09:10Z (canary). No errors logged at infra layer during that window.
dev_kate: if they still see 403 with correct headers, we need server-side logs for that request-id. sara, can you request the log bundle and give me the x-request-id value + approximate timestamp? I'll pull logs and compare computed signature vs provided.
sara_support: customer already gave x-request-id: req_20270308_9f7c2a and said it happened at approx 09:12am PST. Can you pull logs for that id?
dev_kate: pulled logs: server entry for req_20270308_9f7c2a shows:
```
time=2027-03-08T09:12:15Z request_id=req_20270308_9f7c2a remote_ip=52.10.4.12 method=POST path=/v1/embeddings status=403 reason=signature_mismatch computed_sig=Gzi9... provided_sig=Gzi_-... note="base64 vs urlsafe" user_agent=curl/7.85
```
dev_kate: that note indicates the provided signature had URL-safe characters '-' and '_' where our canonicalization expects '+' and '/'. So the client likely used urlsafe_b64 when canonicalizing. We accept both normally, but during rotation we had a codepath that enforced standard base64 for one traffic lane — likely a canary bug.
sara_support: Can we confirm fix? dev_kate: yes patch queued to normalize both forms at authentication layer. I've opened an internal PR and flagged as P0 for rollback if needed. For now workaround for customer: re-encode the signature to standard base64 before sending — easiest is to ensure their signing library uses standard base64 encoding (not urlsafe). For curl users, if they're constructing auth tokens manually, ensure any base64 uses + and / not - and _. Alternatively use the official SDK which does correct encoding.
sara_support: please send this to customer and ask them to test the small change (we can test together). Also ask for any additional request-ids if there are multiple failures.
customer_acme: thanks, we'll try re-encoding and report back in ~30m. Appreciate the quick triage.
raj_oncall: add note to incident tracker: INC-2027-0312-key-rotation-b64-canary. tagging eng-runtime and eng-security. If we see >5 customers, we'll trigger rollback.
sara_support: closing loop for now, will re-open thread if customer still sees failures. :thumbsup!
